Gaethje later revealed he strayed from the original game plan in the opening round while searching for a knockout, prompting his corner to slow him down. Even so, the early damage proved pivotal. Pimblett admitted a crushing body shot in Round 1 shifted the momentum, yet he dug deep and survived all five rounds, earning respect from fans and Gaethje alike.

The championship rounds evolved into a full‑scale war, with both men exchanging heavy shots until the final buzzer. As the arena erupted, Gaethje and Pimblett shared a moment of respect following a brutal and unforgettable contest.

The victory pushes Gaethje’s record to 27‑5, giving him four wins in his last five outings, while Pimblett suffers his first defeat in ten fights, dropping to 23‑4 but gaining admiration for his grit and toughness.

Sean O’Malley stepped back into the Octagon and put on a poised, high‑level performance against Song Yadong, earning a unanimous decision win in the UFC 324 co‑main event at T‑Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. After three closely contested rounds, all three judges scored the fight 29‑28 for O’Malley, as “Sugar” displayed sharp footwork, precise timing, and elite striking awareness. #UFC324 #SeanOMalley #SongYadong

Right from the opening moments, O’Malley controlled the distance with smooth movement, circling the cage while mixing jabs, teeps, and body shots to keep Song off balance. Song answered back by attacking the legs and pushing forward, briefly securing a takedown late in Round 1 to keep the fight competitive.

title: What Jews In Hollywood Are Finally Saying Out Loud
description:
In the aftermath of the horror of Oct. 7, 2023, one of the most discouraging things for embattled American Jews was the relative silence from Hollywood. An industry that was never slow to speak up about all sorts of other causes and filled with Jewish artists seemed curiously unconcerned about the assault on Israel and the subsequent surge of antisemitism. As JNS editor-in-chief Jonathan Tobin says, American Jews were left to wonder why the arts community seemed just as likely to cheer for those attacking Israel as to declare their solidarity with Jewish hostages.

He’s joined in this week’s episode of Think Twice by actor, singer and director Jonah Platt who has dedicated his energies since Oct. 7 to advocating for Jewish solidarity and unity. Platt, the son of a successful film producer and philanthropist, hosts a podcast called “Being Jewish With Jonah Platt,” points out that most of those Jews who have remained silent were never engaged or committed Jewishly. Nevertheless, he says the failure of those who had often called upon the Jewish community to offer them solidarity on other issues but were then not willing to do so when the Jews needed help after Oct. 7 was noticed. Platt noted that there were people who in the second week of October couldn't put their names on a letter saying free the hostages because they couldn't get involved. “That, I'll never understand and to me that's pretty inexcusable,” he said.

But, he adds, no one should be shocked when those Jewish artists who never opened their mouths on behalf of the Jewish people on a good day didn’t suddenly open their mouths on a really terrible day.

Platt says that those who run the entertainment business are generally worried about politics becoming part of the conversation about their work. Nevertheless, he pointed out that there is no “blacklisting” of pro-Israel artists in Hollywood. Those who have spoken up for Israel like actress Jennifer Goodwin, who appeared on Platt’s podcast, haven’t suffered in their careers.

Nevertheless, the erasure of Jews from the movies is, he thinks, “an inherited ethos” from the 1930s when the Jewish founders of Hollywood were desperate to assimilate and to avoid the antisemitism of that era. 

Another problem is that even many of those artists who don’t hesitate to identify Jewishly define themselves largely by the ideas of social justice and solidarity with others rather than advocating for Jewish causes. In this way, they are uncomfortable about supporting Israel and Israeli victims without also expressing sympathy for Arabs who have suffered as a result of a war their side started.

With respect to how Jewish families can deal with divisions caused by some family members who have taken sides against Israel, Platt says the most important thing is to preserve relationships with loved ones while being honest about those differences. In this he speaks with experience because his brother, actor Ben Platt has spoken up on behalf of the Palestinians and against Israel.

As for how the community as a whole should deal with those who oppose Israel’s existence, he takes a very different view. He believes there should be room for questions and debate and criticisms of Israel’s government, especially for young people and others who are not fully educated about the issues. But we shouldn’t have to debate about whether we ought to be connected with Israel.

title: The Hidden Power Structure Behind Israel's Political Crisis
description:
With Israelis set to go to the polls in a few months, an issue that has been on the backburner since Oct. 7 will probably again be provoking public debate in the Jewish state. An effort to reform Israel’s Supreme Court and judicial system enraged the opponents of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government in 2023 and is likely to be on the agenda again. Joining JNS editor-in-chief Jonathan Tobin in this week’s episode of Think Twice is Israel-American lawyer Yonatan Green, author of the new book, Rogue Justice: The Rise of Judicial Supremacy In Israel.

Green says that there is no court in the world in a democratic country that has the kind of power that Israel’s Supreme Court has seized for itself. And contrary to the claims of the opponents of judicial reform, “the biggest threat to Israeli democracy and the rule of law is the Israeli Supreme Court itself and its allies and its proxies.”

By abolishing the very notions of standing and justiciability, two cornerstones of English and American law, Israel’s courts have arrogated to themselves the ability to overrule the elected government on virtually any issue or action in ways unheard of in other democracies. This has created a system of judicial supremacy that is antithetical to democracy. And when you add in the fact that members of the court have the power to name or at least veto potential fellow judges, what Israel has created is a judicial oligarchy.

Nevertheless, judicial reform opponents call any effort to rein in this undemocratic system and re-establish a balance between the judiciary and the elected members of the Knesset and government a threat to democracy. Green believes that many Israelis believe this to be true because when it comes to the judiciary, citizens of the Jewish state are essentially isolated from other democratic nations and have no idea what is considered normative elsewhere.

As a result, they actually believe that democracy is not a matter of majority rule limited by independent courts that are restrained from overstepping their responsibilities. Rather, they actually are under the impression, reinforced by liberal dominance of their education system, that the rule of elites who have the right and duty to ignore the will of the voters is democracy. Moreover, they seem unfamiliar with the basic concept underlying the American system which holds that the rights of citizens are derived from God rather than a gift from a government that can be limited or taken away at will.

Green believes the danger from this undemocratic and coercive system that pretends to be democratic but is not, goes beyond the impact of an out-of-control judiciary. It has also increased polarization and made it harder for Israelis to get along with each other.

The solution to this problem, he says, is a much-needed change in Israeli education to promote knowledge about how democracy works and the election of a constitutional convention that, like the one that wrote America’s constitution in 1787, can come up with a more equitable system.

title: Building a Sweet Marriage/Family||Pastor Sarah Omakwu  || FIRST SERVICE || 14062026
description:
Genesis 2:18-25; Matthew 19:3-9; Ephesians 5:21-31; Phillipians 2:1-4
If you follow the scripture, you will have a sweet home. Marriage is looking out for the other person's interest. A sweet marriage starts by making good decisions. 
Good Decisions in Marriage
1. Make a decision that your home will be a haven, where people run back for peace, love, attention, and care. 
2. Your home should be Christ-centered. Jesus must be the Lord of your home. 
3. Look at what the Bible says about marriage and a godly family. 
4. Live by the Holy Spirit and not the flesh. 
By these decisions, you set your marriage on a firm foundation that cannot be moved. Make Jesus the centre of your values and decisions, knowing that you are his ambassador on earth. Jeremiah 29:11.
God's plan is that the home will be the place where his plan is revealed. In the family, the man creates the atmosphere where people experience the peace of God. Your home is not supposed to be a war zone. 
In God's plan, man is supposed to bring this Scripture to being. You are supposed to be a replica of God to your children.
In a God-centered marriage, men and women are equal. The female was already in the man before she was created. They are equal in worth before God. Galatians 3:28. 
A key is not more important than a padlock and vice-versa, and soup was not made to be eaten alone. Man and woman were created to be interdependent; one can't survive without the other. The wife makes the home flow.

description:
FWC Lawsuit Update

A hearing was held before Judge John C. Cooper on the Parties' reciprocal motions for summary judgment in USARK Florida's lawsuit against FWC. 

Following a discussion about procedural issues involving record evidence, the Court continued the matter until September 7, to allow FWC the opportunity to provide citations in support of its legal argument.

FWC's enforcement of "Prohibited Species" rules has led to the confiscation and euthanasia of animals as well as the destruction of small businesses.

Conditional Species regulations, which were created with input of reptile keepers in 2010, were successful in preventing escapes and releases. 

In 2021, FWC rejected the input of reptile keepers and moved Green iguanas, tegus, Nile monitors, Green Anacondas, and the larger pythons, to the “Prohibited Species” list, which prompted this lawsuit.

Judge Cooper has allowed USARK FL to argue that FWC lacks the constitutional authority to regulate captive animals.

title: Brazil 🇧🇷 vs Canada 🇨🇦 | Highlights | Men's VNL 2026
description:
Brazil vs Canada | Highlights | Men's VNL 2026. Brazil 🇧🇷 defeated Canada 🇨🇦 in one of the most thrilling matches of Week 2 of the 2026 FIVB Volleyball Nations League, surviving an incredible five-set battle in Ljubljana, Slovenia. After nearly three hours of high-level volleyball, Brazil emerged victorious 3-2 (25-17, 23-25, 28-26, 22-25, 17-15), snapping its three-match losing streak and earning a much-needed victory in the race for the VNL Finals.

Brazil started the match in dominant fashion, taking the opening set 25-17 with powerful serving, solid blocking, and efficient attacking. Canada quickly recovered in the second set, improving its reception and side-out game to claim a hard-fought 25-23 victory and level the match at one set apiece.

The third set became the turning point of the contest. Both teams traded points throughout an intense battle that featured several set points on both sides. Brazil eventually held its nerve to edge the marathon set 28-26, taking a 2-1 lead.

Canada refused to give up and produced another impressive comeback in the fourth set. Strong performances from Sharone Vernon-Evans and Skyler Varga helped the Canadians win 25-22 and force a deciding fifth set.

The tiebreak delivered even more drama. Neither team managed to pull away as momentum shifted repeatedly during the closing rallies. Brazil's experience proved decisive in the final moments, as the South Americans converted one of their late match points to secure a dramatic 17-15 victory.

Canada's offense was led by Sharone Vernon-Evans, who finished with 19 points, including two service aces, while Skyler Varga added 18 points with 15 kills, two aces, and one block. Brazil relied on a balanced offensive performance, with setter Fernando "Cachopa" Kreling expertly distributing the ball and helping multiple attackers score in key moments throughout the match.

Although the statistics were closely matched, Brazil proved slightly more composed during the biggest moments of the contest. Winning the crucial third set 28-26 and the deciding fifth set 17-15 ultimately made the difference between victory and defeat.

This victory was especially important for Brazil, ending a difficult stretch of three consecutive defeats during the Ljubljana leg of the tournament and keeping its hopes of qualifying for the Volleyball Nations League Finals alive. For Canada, the loss was another heartbreaking result, marking its fourth straight defeat of Week 2 despite producing one of its strongest performances of the competition.

Match Result:
🇧🇷 Brazil 3-2 Canada 🇨🇦

Set Scores:
25-17, 23-25, 28-26, 22-25, 17-15

Top Scorers:
🇨🇦 Sharone Vernon-Evans – 19 points
🇨🇦 Skyler Varga – 18 points

Competition:
2026 FIVB Volleyball Nations League – Men's Tournament
Week 2 – Pool 6
Arena Stožice, Ljubljana, Slovenia

Brazil finally returned to winning ways after an unforgettable five-set thriller, while Canada once again demonstrated its fighting spirit despite falling just short in one of the best matches of Week 2.

description:
Poland vs Argentina | Highlights | Men's VNL 2026. Poland 🇵🇱 vs. Argentina 🇦🇷 | Highlights | Week 2 | Men's Volleyball Nations League 2026

Defending Volleyball Nations League champions Poland completed their Week 2 campaign with a hard-fought 3-1 victory over Argentina in one of the most entertaining matches of the 2026 VNL. Played on June 28 in front of more than 11,000 fans in Gliwice, Poland, the home team had to recover after losing an unforgettable opening set before taking control of the match and securing another important win in the race for the VNL Finals.

The match immediately made Volleyball Nations League history thanks to an extraordinary first set that Argentina won 50-48. The opening set lasted far longer than a typical volleyball set, with both teams saving multiple set points and exchanging spectacular rallies before Argentina finally converted one of their opportunities. With a combined 98 points, the set became the highest-scoring set ever played in Volleyball Nations League history.

Argentina entered the match full of confidence and showed excellent volleyball from the very beginning. Their aggressive serving, disciplined blocking, and efficient transition offense allowed them to challenge one of the world's strongest teams despite playing away from home. After winning the historic opening set, Argentina looked capable of pulling off one of the biggest upsets of Week 2.

Poland, however, responded like true defending champions. Instead of allowing the heartbreaking first set to affect their performance, they immediately raised their level in every aspect of the game. The second set proved just as dramatic, with Poland narrowly escaping 26-24 after another tense finish. Winning that crucial second set completely changed the momentum of the match.

From that point onward, Poland controlled the contest much more comfortably. Their blocking became more effective, their serves placed increasing pressure on Argentina's reception, and their attack operated with greater efficiency. Poland won the third set 25-19 before closing the fourth 25-20 to complete an impressive comeback victory.

One of Poland's biggest strengths throughout the match was the depth of their roster. Even after the exhausting opening set, they continued rotating fresh attackers while maintaining a consistently high level of serving, blocking, and defense. Their patience during long rallies gradually wore Argentina down both physically and mentally.

Although Argentina suffered another defeat, the South Americans delivered one of their strongest performances of the tournament. They matched Poland for long stretches, played fearless volleyball, and demonstrated once again why they remain one of the toughest opponents in international volleyball. However, maintaining the same level after the emotionally draining opening sets proved impossible against the defending champions.

The victory improved Poland's overall Volleyball Nations League record to 6-2 after two weeks of competition, strengthening their position in the standings and bringing them another step closer to qualification for the 2026 VNL Finals. Argentina dropped to 2-6, making their road to the Finals significantly more difficult.

Combined with Poland's remarkable comeback and the electric atmosphere inside the arena, the match will undoubtedly be remembered as one of the greatest encounters of the 2026 VNL season.

title: Japan 🇯🇵 vs Serbia 🇷🇸 | Highlights | Men's VNL 2026
description:
Japan vs Serbia | Highlights | Men's VNL 2026. The second week of the qualifying round of the "Volleyball Nations League 2026" (VNL) took place in Orleans, France, starting on Wednesday, June 24th.

The Japanese men's volleyball team, ranked 5th in the FIVB world rankings (as of the start of the match), faced Serbia, ranked 9th, on Wednesday, June 24th Japan time, and won in sets 3-1 (25-17, 25-15, 22-25, 25-16), bringing their overall record to 5 wins and 0 losses.

In the first set, Japan's first point came with a back attack by Yuji Nishida. They then broke serve again after Taishi Onodera's serve to take a 5-2 lead. With stable serve reception, they launched a variety of attacks, and Onodera's quick attack and Yuki Ishikawa's back attack from a rally secured the lead for Japan. After that, they continued to score points with Nishida's soft shots and extended their lead to 16-9. Then, Shoma Tomita, who came in as a relief server, scored a service ace, and Japan, who had led throughout the set, won the first set 25-17.

The second set started with Ishikawa scoring with a high set. Ishikawa's serve was in good form, and consecutive points were scored against them. Then, Onodera made a block and a good receive, giving them a big lead of 18-8. At the end, Onodera scored with a quick attack to win the set 25-15.

In the third set, Ishikawa's spike got Japan off to a good start, but Serbia's blocks caught up with the score, putting Japan behind 3-6 in the early stages. Japan scored points through tenacious defense, and after making a double substitution with Miyaura Kento and Nagaro Motoki, they gradually gained momentum. Evadedan Larry's block narrowed the gap to one point, but Serbia broke through with blocks, and Japan lost the set 22-25.

In the fourth set, Ishikawa's service ace and Takahashi Ran's block gave Japan a 6-3 lead. Serbia broke the serve and seemed to be shifting the momentum, but Takahashi Ran inspired the team with a powerful back attack and a service ace, extending the lead to 14-7. Serbia scored another service ace, but Takahashi Ran made a block to make it 19-12, prompting Serbia to call a timeout. Japan continued to score points, and finally Miyaura scored the winning point to secure the set 25-16, winning the set 3-1.

The Japanese men's national team will play their next match against Iran (ranked 17th) on Friday, June 26th at 24:00. Can they achieve a sixth consecutive win against their Asian rivals? Please continue to support the Japanese men's national team.

title: #movie PRISON BREAK – Bellick Crosses the Line: T-Bag's Darkest Trigger Revealed
description:
In the brutal, tension-filled world of Prison Break, few characters are as terrifying, unpredictable, and strangely compelling as Theodore "T-Bag" Bagwell. Played with chilling brilliance by Robert Knepper, T-Bag is a racist, manipulative, cold-blooded killer who has survived everything Fox River State Penitentiary could throw at him. He's cunning, vicious, and seemingly untouchable. But even the most hardened criminals have cracks in their armor – and in one unforgettable scene, we see exactly where T-Bag's deepest wound lies.

The scene unfolds in the prison yard or hallway, where T-Bag is locked in a tense conversation with Captain Brad Bellick – the sadistic, power-hungry guard who loves nothing more than tormenting the inmates under his watch. Bellick, ever the bully, starts with his usual sneering insults, trying to chip away at T-Bag's confidence. But T-Bag, as always, fires back with his trademark venom, twisting his words into razor-sharp barbs that cut deeper than any shiv. He mocks Bellick's authority, his failed career, his pathetic need to feel powerful behind a badge. It's classic T-Bag – cruel, clever, and completely in control.

But then Bellick plays his trump card. With a smug, malicious grin, he brings up T-Bag's birth – the circumstances of his abandonment, his mother's prostitution, and the fact that he never knew his real father. title: FKG Group - Glen Niven Dam Upgrade - Blast Footage
description:
The FKG Group was recently engaged to increase the spillway capacity of the Glen Niven Dam and upgrade the dam embankment. During the project, the civil team carried out a blast for excavation of approximately 6,000m3 of granite material to form part of an enlarged primary spillway for the dam. The blasted material was then processed and repurposed as scour protection in the terminal section of the primary spillway, a rock deflection wall on the auxiliary spillway, rip rap on the upstream face of the embankment, and general fill. title: What CFMF Means To Me | EOFY Appeal
description:
What difference does the Centre for Men & Families make?

Rather than hearing it from us, hear it from the men whose lives have been impacted by this work.

In this short video, men from around Australia share, in their own words, how CFMF has helped them navigate addiction, relationship breakdown, isolation, grief, shame, mental health struggles, and life's biggest challenges.

They speak about finding friendship where there was loneliness, hope where there was despair, and a community where they could finally be seen, heard, accepted, and supported.

These stories remind us why this work matters.

As we approach the end of the financial year, we invite you to consider supporting CFMF so that more men can access counselling, circles, rites of passage, retreats, and the kind of life-changing community these men describe.

Every donation helps ensure that no man has to walk alone.

To make a tax-deductible donation, visit:
https://www.givenow.com.au/eofyappealcfmf

title: Tayo Aina
I Found the African City Hidden Inside America
description:
I Found the African City Hidden Inside America is a video about my exploration of one of America's most distinctive cities: New Orleans

Everyone knows New Orleans for Mardi Gras, jazz, and Bourbon Street. But nobody told me that buried underneath the party, hidden in the food, the music, the culture, and the very soul of this city, is Africa. New Orleans is unlike anywhere else in America. And once you understand WHY, you'll never see it the same way again.

In this episode of Beyond Borders, I explore the city that should technically not exist — a city shaped more by African hands, African traditions, and African spirit than any other place in the United States. From Congo Square, where enslaved Africans preserved their culture through music and dance, to the Creole culture that blended African, French, and Caribbean influences into something entirely its own — New Orleans is Africa hiding in plain sight.

We eat the food, walk the streets, feel the energy, and ask the real questions: How did Africa end up inside America? And what does New Orleans tell us about who we really are?

This is Beyond Borders. We don't just travel. We discover.

title: EYIMOFE (This is My Desire) | Trailer
description:
Set in Lagos, Nigeria Eyimofe (This is My Desire) follows the stories of Mofe, a factory technician, and Rosa, a hairdresser, on their quest for what they believe will be a better life on foreign shores. 

A passport, photos and a visa form recurring elements. The characters’ misfortunes are part of their everyday life and they are sketching out the need to leave Nigeria at the same time. At the bottom of the socio-economic ladder, status, money, gender, skin colour and family structures are inextricably connected. The longing for another life is but one thread in this complex mesh, a promise that floats above things at once near and far away. #EYIMOFE
